title: Power Apps: build model-driven apps with Copilot Cowork
summary: Hold: the briefing reports Cowork's acting identity as undocumented, although Microsoft's Cowork guidance says every action is authorized through the user's Microsoft 365 account. The roadmap facts and published control paths and commands are supported; the skill's specific Dataverse connection mechanism remains undocumented.

claims.where: Why it matters; Cost and licensing; Scope; controls[0].note; Governance controls
claims.claim: Users in scope of a spending policy selecting Cowork have Cowork access.
claims.quote: Any user in the scope of a spending policy that selects Cowork can use Cowork, regardless of how small the credit limit is.

claims.where: Cost and licensing; controls[0].note; Governance guidance; Governance controls
claims.claim: A low credit limit does not prevent Cowork access.
claims.quote: A policy with a limit of one credit still grants access. To remove access for a user, remove them from every spending policy that includes Cowork. A low credit limit doesn't block access.

claims.claim: A Cowork-selecting spending policy can be scoped to a security group for a pilot.
claims.quote:
On the Scope user and group step, choose Specific groups and select the security group.
On the Select agents and services step, select Cowork.

claims.claim: Removing a user from every spending policy that includes Cowork removes their access.
claims.quote: To remove access for a user, remove them from every spending policy that includes Cowork.

claims.claim: Configuration on the Cowork entry under Agents > All Agents has no effect on who can use Cowork.
claims.quote: The Cowork agent entry is still visible under Agents > All Agents, but any configuration on it has no effect on who can use Cowork.

claims.claim: Credit limits are not a real-time access gate, so users may start tasks after reaching a limit.
claims.quote: Credit consumption and limit enforcement are evaluated asynchronously, so a user might be able to start one or more tasks after their limit is reached before enforcement takes effect.

claims.claim: The spending-policy path is Copilot > Cost Management > Configuration > + Add spending policy > Identity > Specific groups > Select agents and services > Cowork > Set limits and alerts.
claims.quote:
go to Copilot > Cost Management.
Select the Configuration tab and then select + Add spending policy.
choose Identity as the scope.
switch to Specific groups
Select agents and services
Set limits and alerts

claims.claim: POST /beta/copilot/costManagement/spendingPolicies creates a spending policy with service settings and credit limits, initially disabled as the note explains.
claims.quote:
POST https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/copilot/costManagement/spendingPolicies

Required properties are displayName, periodLimit, perUserLimit, and serviceSettings.

New policies are created disabled.

claims.claim: The create API supports serviceSettings with serviceId cowork and state enabled, plus periodLimit and perUserLimit.
claims.quote:
Required properties are displayName, periodLimit, perUserLimit, and serviceSettings.

{ "serviceId": "cowork", "state": "enabled" }

claims.claim: New group spending policies are disabled and their audience should be linked before the service enables them.
claims.quote: A new policy is created disabled. For a group-scoped policy, follow the safe-create sequence: create the policy disabled, link its audience with Add assigned group, and let the service enable it once its requirements are satisfied.

claims.claim: The general plugin-blocking path is Agents > Tools > plugin > Users > Block in the Microsoft 365 admin center.
claims.quote:
select Agents > Tools.
Find the plugin you want to manage and go to the Users tab.
Select Block: No users in your tenant can access the plugin.

claims.claim: POST https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/copilot/admin/catalog/packages/{id}/block blocks a Copilot package.
claims.quote:

POST https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/copilot/admin/catalog/packages/{id}/block

claims.claim: The security-role path is Manage > Environments > environment > Settings > Users + permissions > Users > user > Manage security roles in the Power Platform admin center.
claims.quote:
select Manage.
select Environments, and then select an environment from the list.
Select Settings.
Select Users + permissions, and then select Users.
On the Users page select a user, and then select Manage security roles.

claims.claim: pac admin assign-user --environment <environment-id> --user <upn> --role "<role-name>" assigns a user and security role to the target Dataverse environment.
claims.quote:
Assign a user to a target Dataverse environment with specified security role.
--role: Name or ID of security role to be applied to user
--user: Object ID or user principal name (UPN)
--environment: ID or URL of the environment to assign a user to.

claims.claim: The System Administrator role provides the required security-role-assignment privileges by default.
claims.quote: By default, the System Administrator security role has all the required privileges to assign security roles to any user, including assigning the System Administrator security role.
